summary: V6.7 starts from the V6.6 terminal commit rather than reopening its radius recovery. ALSO, evidence-theory occupancy and SelfOcc motivate reusing the already-stored directional behind-hit ray state, intersected with same-Actor one-voxel support. The repair rule is frozen before the task-untouched cohort is scored.

The frozen head reaches 0.7105/0.7307 AUROC/AUPRC on 517 Actor-units and is above chance in all six scenes without refit. This is sufficient to freeze the matched 50% action set, but the globally consumed cohort still cannot support a fresh V6.7 claim.

V6.7 reuses the audited V6.6 package/action cores behind version-specific runners. The only pending P3 config field is the future P2 canonical run locator; no gate, budget or score changes depend on P2 output.

The package retains all 517 Actor states and complete metadata across 107 Actors with zero removal, zero hidden-target fields and no runtime model or hazard existence gate. P3 now binds only this canonical locator and keeps its fixed 50% budget unchanged.

The frozen 258-action L0 set handles 185 of 295 conflict states while retaining every Actor, hazard proxy and scene. P4 keeps these exact actions and adds only the pre-frozen source behind-hit requirement to one-voxel support.

P4 removes 67.90% of conflict points and preserves all Actor contracts, but overall/clean retention 0.3924/0.3965 misses the frozen 0.40 gates. The aggregated raw-endpoint behind-hit grid is not Actor/ray aligned after hit motion compensation. External ray-occupancy research motivates one target-frame analytic inward-ray recovery without changing radius, actions or gates.

The one structural recovery passes all nine gates: 51.74% conflict reduction with 53.19% clean retention and exact Actor contracts. V67-F01 is resolved. Because this cohort is globally consumed, the method now moves unchanged to the separate V65 P2 cohort for an end-to-end legacy confirmation.

The frozen head remains above deterministic chance in all six scenes and passes 4/4 gates on 570 Actor-units. q0 is about 0.03 stronger in both pooled ranking metrics, so no head-over-q0 generalization claim is made. The confirmation chain proceeds with the preregistered learned arm and reports q0/oracle comparators unchanged.

All 570 Actor states and complete metadata are retained across 119 Actors with zero removals and zero hidden-target fields. The fixed-action audit now binds the P5 and P6 canonical locators without changing the 50% budget.

The frozen L0 arm handles 191/312 conflicts at a 285/570 budget and passes all six gates. q0 is stronger pooled, while L0 exceeds 0.5 reduction in every scene. P8 keeps the preregistered L0 chain and applies the exact P4R physical rule once.

The exact inward-ray rule passes all nine gates on the second legacy cohort with 50.15% conflict reduction and 55.67% clean retention. The two-cohort legacy evidence is now positive. A preregistered unprocessed cohort from unused archive band 4 is required before a fresh empirical claim.

Six new scenes, 72 native targets and 72 evidence units are complete. Native GPU inference overlapped later scene preprocessing. V67-F02 groups launcher-only parent/config/device-index failures before quality read; the successful native aggregate did not repeat inference. The next operation is the frozen-head GPU transfer, not more input audit.

The frozen head passes all ranking gates on 938 fresh Actor-units and all six scenes. q0 has higher AUPRC, so the learned arm is not claimed universally superior. The exact preregistered chain continues to package, actions and physical repair.

All 938 Actor states and metadata are retained across 186 Actors with zero removals, zero hidden-target fields and no runtime model or hazard existence gate. P12 binds the P10/P11 canonical locators at the unchanged 50-percent budget.

The frozen L0 arm handles 341/563 fresh conflicts at the 469/938 budget, slightly exceeding q0 pooled, while retaining every Actor and hazard attribute. A shell run-id quoting error was resolved by renaming the completed directory without repeating evaluation. P13 applies the unchanged physical rule once.

The exact analytic rule passes all nine gates on six newly processed scenes with 52.92 percent conflict reduction and 55.98 percent clean retention. The capability chain is now positive on fresh empirical data. Research moves to a learned residual surface field instead of more legacy confirmation.

The point model memorizes the training residual set and rescues almost every selection rejection, raising clean retention but collapsing conflict reduction to 9.39 percent. Selective-risk research motivates one leave-one-scene-out calibration recovery; the exact action denominator is corrected at the same time without using selection scores to fit the threshold.

Scene-crossfit calibration restores the exact analytic denominator but the final point model remains overconfident and lowers conflict reduction to 23.43 percent. The single point-family recovery is exhausted. Following the preregistered fallback, the next model predicts trajectory-visited state reliability instead of voxel correctness.

The trajectory-level target is learnable in source data, but the free MLP residual overwrites the strong qmean reference and collapses all transfer metrics. One normalized residual recovery replaces scene-sensitive features with twelve case-centered bounded lattice biases while retaining qmean as the dominant score.

The bounded adapter slightly improves all pooled transfer rankings but only adds 0.0066 selected-cost reduction over qmean, below the frozen direct-selection gates. The recovery is exhausted. Both consumed cohorts become development domains for a new model-frozen fresh action-task confirmation on P9.

The model-frozen P9 action read confirms qmean itself is useful but the action-ID adapter loses 0.0012 selected-cost reduction and 0.0447 pairwise concordance. P17 changes representation from action ID to a monotone distributional pool rather than tuning the adapter.

The learned quantile pool transfers better than the free point or trajectory MLPs but consistently degrades the stronger qmean baseline on P9. Score-replacement methods are closed. P18 freezes qmean and learns only case-level authority versus abstention.

Freezing qmean and learning only when to grant authority improves P9 selected-cost reduction by 0.0697 at fixed half-case coverage; 91.4 percent of authorized cases have nonnegative benefit and all six scenes improve. The exact compiler now moves once to an independent legacy cohort.

Relative gain replicates at +0.0558 with all scenes non-increasing, but absolute reduction 0.3509 misses the frozen 0.45 gate. Selective gating is closed without threshold recovery. P20 learns the action set itself with a four-domain differentiable listwise objective.

Directly optimizing differentiable bottom-quartile cost across four domains transfers to an action-task-untouched cohort, improving both pairwise ranking and selected cost over qmean. P21 freezes this ordering and learns only selective authority on five development domains.

On P2V, listwise ordering contributes +0.0590 reduction over qmean and selective authority adds another +0.0460; every authorized case benefits. P22 now adds an unsafe-event selected-set objective and tests once on eight action-task-untouched scenes.

The binary any-hidden-FREE objective adds only 0.0047 unsafe reduction over P20 and slightly degrades mean cost, consistent with a discrete tail barrier. P23 changes the risk object to continuous entropic selected cost on seven domains without sweeping P22.

Entropic training improves mean reduction and pairwise ranking but leaves the selected top tail unchanged. Tail auxiliary families are closed. P24 preserves the supported P20 ranking and learns only cross-case allocation under an exact fixed total budget.

Cross-case calibration raises reduction from fixed P20 0.5968 to 0.7584 with the exact same 222 actions and all evaluable scenes improved. P25 combines this allocation with selective abstention while freezing half-case coverage.

At the exact same 243-action budget, learned abstention plus cross-case allocation covers 60.7 percent of cases and raises reduction from fixed P20 0.3122 and min-one P24 0.5944 to 0.6950; all eight scenes are non-increasing. P26 retains the contract, rolls P4C into development, retrains once, and tests on a larger 16-scene cohort.

On 180 evaluable cases across 15 evaluable scenes, exact-total coverage allocation raises reduction from fixed P20 0.4006 and P24 0.6839 to 0.7925 while covering 64.4 percent of cases. P27 turns global coverage into a per-stratum contract using the same learned offset family.

Per-stratum floors preserve 50--75 percent case coverage in all four contexts while retaining 0.8004 reduction at the exact 222-action budget. P28 makes requested budget fraction an explicit condition and tests interpolation to an unseen one-third budget.

A single model trained at quarter and half budgets transfers to an unseen one-third budget with exact 363 actions, 70.8 percent case coverage, 58.3 percent minimum group coverage, and 0.6749 reduction. P29 enforces nested low/high authority sets to eliminate budget-change discontinuity.

Exact quarter and half budgets retain 0.7589 and 0.3879 reduction while all 243 low-budget actions are preserved in the high-budget set and both budgets improve all eight scenes. P30 moves from budget conditioning to the future-horizon H requested by the trajectory reliability object.

Training with H=1 and H=2 conditions transfers to H=1.5 with exact 176 actions, 63.6 percent case coverage, 0.7407 reduction, and +0.5052 over fixed P20. P31 combines budget and horizon into one task-conditioned authority compiler.

The unseen pair (one-third,H=1.5s) retains exact budget, 72.7 percent case coverage, 58.3 percent minimum group coverage, and 0.6906 reduction. P32 integrates strict nested budgets at the held-out horizon.

At held-out H=1.5, exact quarter and half budgets achieve 0.8110 and 0.4041 reduction with all 176 low-budget actions retained. P33 moves the joint condition once to P4C for a second-cohort replication.

On P4C H=1.5, the unseen one-third budget condition attains exact 315 actions, 69.7 percent case coverage, 0.6982 reduction, and all eight scenes improve. P34 adds bounded aleatoric error scale without reopening failed action-tail auxiliaries or claiming epistemic uncertainty.
